title: Scheduler journal hotfix R3 — bound SSE reads, SQL-filtered cohort scan + bounded integrity sweep, fresh-wake backoff reset (live-ops regression)
description: Live-ops fix for sustained CPU burn + dashboard latency (161k events, ~1.2 cores idle), plus R1-R3 audit corrections. R0: eventsSince pages 'WHERE seq > ? ORDER BY seq LIMIT ?' (store.listEventsSince), per-row hash verification preserved; settle() wait_streak decays empty timed-wait polls by min(2^streak,12). R1-F1: observe()/accountWake() post-dedup writes reset next_due=null + wait_streak=0; settle() clears next_due when pending remains; markDue/duplicates untouched. R1-F2+R2-F1: nextFairCandidate pushes the usability predicate AND active-lease exclusion (NOT EXISTS) into an uncharged SQL filter — unchanged cohorts of ANY size converge to idle silence; charged re-proofs only on shortlisted rows; FAIR_VISIT on usable finds, FAIR_ROUND on wrap/bound refresh preserved. R3-F1: the SQL filter excluded rows before readSchedulerRow could verify them, so a bounded amortized integrity sweep now runs on the idle path — tier 1 screens every WAKE_STATE/LEASE_STATE row's commit-ledger vs entity version via one uncharged aggregate (catches canonical-put-without-commit and forged rows, valid hash included); tier 2 deep-verifies a rotating <=16-row slice through full charged readSchedulerRow (payload hash + commit chain) via a process-local coverage cursor; suspects are confirmed and journaled once as dedup'd INTEGRITY_FAULT receipts, and shortlist re-proof failures fault+skip instead of aborting the scan. Corrupted rows can never be claimed (claim() still re-proves and throws) but never stay silently hidden. Detection bounds: tier-1 flags on the first idle call; tier-2 covers the keyspace every ceil(rows/16) idle calls. Nothing journaled while the cohort verifies clean. Evidence: 17 hotfix tests failing-first (H7a/h7b silent-hiding, h7c unhandled abort on 96d5f53), all green post-fix; adjacent suites 236/236; tsc clean; build green.
